description:
Meet Tomo, a little blob who lives by your Mac's notch and only speaks Japanese, and only as much as a real child its age.

You never have to remember to study. Every so often while you work, Tomo pops out of the notch with a word or two, then tucks back in. Show it you understood: click the right picture, do what it asks (feed it, put it to bed, give it a hug), or pick what a word means. There's nothing to type and nothing to say out loud, and Tomo says every word for you in Japanese.

Tomo stays out of your way. A visit never takes your keyboard, waits while you're typing and skips when you're away. Close it with × (or Esc once you've clicked it), or just ignore it: Tomo tucks back in with a red dot. No streaks, no guilt. Click small Tomo any time to play.

Your Tomo hatches from an egg the first time you open the app, and no one else's looks quite like it. At 1 year old it says single baby words like ワンワン and バイバイ. Every word you understand helps it grow: it levels up as its words stick, and at each birthday it evolves into a new shape. At 2 it uses two-word phrases, and from 3 it asks you real questions.

A FEW MINUTES A DAY
Tomodachi isn't for cramming. Each word comes back just before you'd forget it: first after a few hours, then days, then weeks. When nothing is due, Tomo rests and tells you when it's back. You can keep practicing, but only answers at the right time move the bar. Growing up takes weeks and months, like a real child.

MADE FOR THE MAC
• A short first run hatches your Tomo, teaches your first word, and asks how often Tomo drops in (every 10 minutes to every 2 hours, or only when you click it), your quiet hours, and whether Tomodachi opens when you log in.
• No visits in your quiet hours (9 PM to 8 AM unless you change them).
• The Tomodachi window: Tomo (its age, level, experience bar and what each age brings), Words (every word with its picture, reading, meaning, stage and when it comes back), Settings and About.
• Menus and shortcuts: Drop in now (⌘D), Tomo's words (⌘W), Settings (⌘,), and a menu bar icon with the same.
• Click a word Tomo says for its card, with the Mac's dictionary a click away.
• On a Mac without a notch, Tomo waits at the top of the screen instead.

THE WORDS
Tomo's words come from research on the words Japanese children understand and say first, in the order they learn them, from baby talk up to six-year-old vocabulary. Meanings come with the app.

PRIVATE AND OFFLINE
No account, no sign-in, no ads, no tracking and no AI. Everything Tomo teaches is in the app, so it works offline. Your progress stays in your own iCloud: with Tomodachi on your iPhone too, signed in to the same iCloud, the two share one Tomo. We run no servers and collect no data.

Tomodachi teaches Japanese to English speakers. Requires macOS 15 or later.
promotionalText: A little blob by your notch who only speaks Japanese, like a real 1-year-old. It drops in with a word while you work, and grows up as you understand it.
reviewNotes:
No sign-in or account is needed. This version teaches Japanese to English speakers; everything it teaches is bundled with the app. It asks for no permissions (no Accessibility, Screen Recording or microphone).

WHERE TOMO APPEARS: Tomo lives at the top of the screen, not in a regular window. On a Mac with a notch, it sits small just left of the notch; when it has a word for you (and when you click it), it opens into a card that hangs from the notch. On a Mac without a notch (or with the lid closed and only an external display), it sits in a small bar at the top centre of the main display and opens from there. Close the card with ×, or with Esc once you've clicked it.

FIRST RUN (about 2 minutes, in a window): tap "Hatch it", answer Tomo's first word by clicking the picture that matches, then choose how often Tomo drops in, quiet hours, and whether Tomodachi opens at login (a switch shown on its own screen; it can be changed later in Settings). Then Tomo pops out of the notch and asks its next word.

THE TOMODACHI WINDOW: click the Dock icon, open the app again, click Tomo's age in the card's header, or use the menu bar icon → Open Tomodachi… (⌘O). Its sidebar has Tomo, Words, Settings and About (version, privacy policy, support, credits). To see a visit right away: Tomo → Drop in now (⌘D), or click small Tomo by the notch.

SPACED REVIEW IS BY DESIGN: after a few answers Tomo rests and says when it's back ("Back at 10:12") and what's left to the next level. This is not a dead end: words come back after hours, then days, as in any spaced-repetition app. Practice stays available on the resting card but doesn't move the bar. To see progress, open Tomo and Words in the window.

PRIVACY: progress syncs between the learner's own devices (another Mac, or the Tomodachi iPhone app) through their private iCloud database (CloudKit). There are no servers of ours, no other network requests (links in About and "Open in Zenbu" open the website in the browser), and no data collected.
